chunks: Ali, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Jameel, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When you are behind an Imam and he recites Al-Hamd and finishes its recitation, you say, 'You are the Praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds', and you do not say 'Ameen'.
ai.seo_question: What should a Shia Muslim say after the Imam finishes reciting Al-Fatiha during prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the distinct Shia jurisprudential practice of reciting Surah Al-Fatiha individually by the follower (ma'mum) during the Imam's recitation, rather than remaining silent or saying 'Ameen'. It highlights the theological emphasis on the follower's active participation in the prayer's recitation, a key differentiator from Sunni schools where the ma'mum often listens silently. This practice underscores the Shia view of the prayer as a personal dialogue with God, even when following an Imam.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Jameel, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Whenever you are behind a prayer-leader, so he recites Al-Hamd (Chapter 1) from its recitations, so say, 
‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the worlds’, but you should not say, ‘Ameen’’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali has narrated from his father from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from Jamil who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If you are behind an Imam when he completes reading al-Hamd you say, ‘all praise belongs to Allah, Cherisher of the worlds,’ and do not say ‘Amen.’” (Ahadith 4-5 are best explained in the form of fatwa.)
